issues.t: Oil sludge leading to engine failure
issues.sym: Knocking from the top of the engine, a flickering oil light, misfires, stalling, or the engine shutting off and not restarting, usually around 80,000 to 100,000 miles. Some fail with no warning.
issues.why: The 2.7L V6 is known for building up oil sludge that blocks oil flow to the bearings and timing chain. The other Stratus engines are not affected the same way.
issues.next: Change oil every 3,000 to 5,000 miles and never ignore an oil light. If the engine knocks, stop and have oil pressure checked; a failed engine is usually replaced.

issues.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: Coolant level drops with no outside leak, milky oil on the dipstick, overheating, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: The 2.7L's water pump is inside the engine behind the timing cover, so a failed seal lets coolant leak into the oil.
issues.next: Stop driving if coolant is vanishing or the oil looks milky. Pump replacement means opening the timing cover, so timing chain parts are often replaced too.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch or breakage
issues.sym: Rattling or clanging from the engine, low oil pressure, stalling, or sudden engine failure.
issues.why: Sludge and poor oil flow wear out the 2.7L's timing chain and its guides.
issues.next: Have a new rattle checked right away; fixing a stretched chain early can prevent engine damage.

issues.t: Head gasket leaks
issues.sym: Oil or coolant leaking from the engine, overheating, white smoke, coolant loss, or oil on the spark plugs.
issues.why: Head gaskets on the Chrysler 2.0L and 2.4L 4-cylinders are a very common complaint, especially on the first-generation cars; owners report some factory gaskets were too thin.
issues.next: Do not keep driving an engine that is overheating. A pressure test and combustion leak test confirm the gasket; the head should be checked for warping.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failure
issues.sym: Slipping, jerking or harsh shifts, a check engine light, getting stuck in one gear, or losing forward and reverse altogether, often around 80,000 miles.
issues.why: Internal wear, a failing pump, burnt clutches or torque converter trouble in the automatic transaxle.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have codes read. Use the exact fluid type the manual lists. A failed unit usually needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Engine stalls while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or at idle, sputters, loses power or won't restart, sometimes worse in hot weather.
issues.why: Many causes are reported, including crank sensor and wiring faults, fuel delivery problems and overheating, and owners often struggle to get a firm diagnosis.
issues.next: Pull over safely if it stalls. Have codes read right after it happens, and ask the shop to check the crank sensor, wiring and fuel pressure.

issues.t: Timing belt failure if replacement is overdue
issues.sym: Usually no warning: the engine suddenly stops and won't restart. Engine damage can follow.
issues.why: Every Stratus engine except the 2.7L V6 uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule.
issues.next: If there is no record of a belt change by about 60,000 to 100,000 miles (check your manual), have the belt, tensioner and usually the water pump replaced.

issues.t: Engine oil leaks
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell, or oil dripping onto the exhaust.
issues.why: Oil leaks from gaskets and seals are common on the first-generation cars, including from the cylinder head oil plug.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the leak traced; oil on a hot exhaust can smoke or catch fire.

issues.t: Blower fan only works on high
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan works only on the highest setting, or not at all.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor burns out or corrodes, sometimes because a worn blower motor draws too much current.
issues.next: Replace the blower motor resistor; if it fails again soon, replace the blower motor too.

issues.t: Temperature control knob breaks
issues.sym: The heater temperature selector stops changing between hot and cold.
issues.why: The temperature blend control breaks.
issues.next: Have the HVAC control and blend door checked.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint wear
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, wandering steering or uneven tire wear. A separated joint can let the wheel collapse.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints lose their grease and wear out; Chrysler recalled some early cars over this.
issues.next: Have the ball joints checked for play at every tire rotation, and replace worn ones right away.

issues.t: Dashboard curls up under the windshield
issues.sym: The top of the dash shrinks and lifts near the windshield, so vents and speaker covers no longer fit.
issues.why: The dashboard material shrinks with heat and age.
issues.next: A dealer can replace the dash, but it is a big job because of the passenger airbag. A dash cover is another option.

issues.t: Water on the passenger floor from a clogged A/C drain
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the front passenger side, often after using the A/C.
issues.why: The A/C evaporator drain tube clogs, so condensation backs up into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the drain tube cleared; dry the carpet to prevent mildew.

issues.t: Transmission won't engage on cold mornings
issues.sym: On cold mornings the car won't go into gear right away, with some slipping or clunking.
issues.why: Owners of both the coupe and sedan report this; dealers have had trouble reproducing it.
issues.next: Note the temperature and conditions when it happens and have the fluid level and condition checked.

issues.t: Lower control arm ball joint can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end; in the worst case the ball joint separates and steering is lost.
issues.why: Ball joints could lose lubrication. Dealers test the seal and replace the control arm if needed.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was completed.

issues.t: Cylinder head oil plug can leak and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the engine, smoke, or a burning smell.
issues.why: An oil galley plug in the cylinder head may not seal or stay in place. Dealers add a new plug and a retaining bracket.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for this recall; many owners report oil loss from this plug.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak (recall)
issues.sym: The brake warning light comes on or the pedal feels low.
issues.why: The master cylinder can leak fluid, weakening half of the brake system.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have a dealer check this recall and inspect the brakes.

issues.t: ABS valve can stick and pull the car (recall)
issues.sym: The car pulls to one side during a hard straight stop.
issues.why: Corrosion in the ABS hydraulic unit can make a front-wheel valve stick.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the recall status.

issues.t: Hood may not stay closed (recall)
issues.sym: The hood is held only by the safety catch and could fly up.
issues.why: If the secondary latch catches without the main latch, the hood is not held properly.
issues.next: Make sure the hood is fully latched and check the recall.

issues.t: Shifter interlock can let the car roll away (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter can leave Park with the key out, or the key comes out when not in Park.
issues.why: The ignition-park interlock can stop working. Two recalls covered it.
issues.next: Use the parking brake and have a dealer confirm the recalls were done.

issues.t: Rear brake lines can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking near the rear wheels, a low pedal or longer stops.
issues.why: A rear brake tube can leak, cutting braking on half of the split system.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have a dealer check the recall status.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaks, a whine from the pump, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The high-pressure power steering hose can age early and leak onto hot parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have a dealer replace the hose under the recall if not already done.

issues.t: Front brake line bracket can break (recall)
issues.sym: No warning until a brake line leaks; then the pedal sinks and stops get longer.
issues.why: A bracket weld can separate and damage the right-front brake tube.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check the recall status.

issues.t: Fuel tank straps can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom at first; a loose tank can rattle or sag.
issues.why: The straps holding the fuel tank were not protected from corrosion and can loosen.
issues.next: Check the recall status.

issues.t: Child seat anchors may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; a child seat may not stay properly attached in a crash.
issues.why: The child seat anchor system did not meet the federal standard.
issues.next: If you use a child seat, have a dealer confirm this recall.

issues.t: Crank sensor wiring can short and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine dies while driving.
issues.why: The crank sensor wiring can rub on a heat shield and short out.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have a dealer re-route the harness under the recall.

issues.t: Transmission cooler hoses can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid drips, poor shifting, or smoke if fluid hits the exhaust.
issues.why: Some transmission cooler hoses were built with a weak inner wall.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the hoses if not already done.

issues.t: Loose steering gear nut (recall)
issues.sym: Steering wheel vibration or stiff steering; in the worst case the car won't steer left.
issues.why: A nut in the steering gear was not tightened properly at the factory.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the steering gear under the recall.

issues.t: Sun visor can break loose in an airbag deployment (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: The passenger sun visor can come off and fly rearward if the passenger airbag deploys. Dealers add a tether strap.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Fuel pump return line can break and leak, coupe (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or fuel leaking under the car.
issues.why: On some 2004 Stratus coupes the return line fitting on the fuel pump was molded poorly and can break.
issues.next: Don't drive it if you smell fuel; have the dealer replace the pump under the recall.
